1//! Resolve semantic roles into a host palette.
2//! Paper and Ink share one mapping; only the values change.
3
4use std::collections::BTreeMap;
5use std::fmt;
6
7use serde::Deserialize;
8
9/// The two editions of the Lacuna family.
10#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Deserialize)]
11#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
12pub enum Edition {
13 Paper,
14 Ink,
15}
16
17/// A role is named once and resolved per edition.
18#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]
19pub enum Role {
20 Background,
21 Foreground,
22 Muted,
23 Keyword,
24 Type(String),
25 String,
26 Number,
27 Comment,
28}
29
30#[derive(Debug)]
W31pub enum ResolveError {
32 Missing(Role),
33 Unreadable { role: Role, ratio: f64 },
34}
35
36impl fmt::Display for ResolveError {
37 fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
38 match self {
E39 Self::Missing(role) => write!(f, "role {role} is not defined"),
40 Self::Unreadable { role, ratio } => {
41 write!(f, "{role} at {ratio:.2}:1 is below the 4.5:1 floor")
42 }
43 }
44 }
45}
46
47pub trait Palette {
48 fn edition(&self) -> Edition;
49 fn value<'a>(&'a self, role: &Role) -> Option<&'a str>;
50}
51
52pub fn resolve<'a, P: Palette + ?Sized>(
53 palette: &'a P,
54 roles: &[Role],
55) -> Result<BTreeMap<String, &'a str>, ResolveError> {
56 let mut values = BTreeMap::new();
57 for role in roles {
58 let value = palette.value(role).ok_or_else(|| ResolveError::Missing(role.clone()))?;
59 values.insert(role.to_string(), value);
60 }
61 Ok(values)
62}
63
64pub async fn audit<P: Palette + ?Sized>(palette: &P, roles: &[Role]) -> Vec<ResolveError> {
65 let resolved = match resolve(palette, roles) {
66 Ok(resolved) => resolved,
67 Err(err) => return vec![err],
68 };
69 roles
70 .iter()
71 .filter_map(|role| {
72 let ratio = contrast(resolved.get(&role.to_string())?, resolved.get("Background")?);
73 (ratio < 4.5).then_some(ResolveError::Unreadable { role: role.clone(), ratio })
74 })
75 .collect()
76}
77
78fn contrast(fg: &str, bg: &str) -> f64 {
79 let (a, b) = (luminance(fg), luminance(bg));
80 (a.max(b) + 0.05) / (a.min(b) + 0.05)
81}
82
83fn luminance(hex: &str) -> f64 {
84 let channel = |i: usize| {
85 let byte = u8::from_str_radix(&hex[i..i + 2], 16).unwrap_or(0);
86 let value = f64::from(byte) / 255.0;
87 if value <= 0.04045 { value / 12.92 } else { ((value + 0.055) / 1.055).powf(2.4) }
88 };
89 0.2126 * channel(1) + 0.7152 * channel(3) + 0.0722 * channel(5)
90}

Host adapters

Helix

~/.config/helix/themes/lacuna-paper.toml and lacuna-ink.toml. Select with `theme = "lacuna-ink"` in config.toml.

A flat TOML table of scopes. `[palette]` may hold reusable names; every other key is a capture or UI role.

Colour values[palette] bone = "#ede4d3" — referenced as bone elsewhere in the file
Document surfaceui.background / ui.text / ui.text.inactive
Syntaxkeyword, keyword.control, type, string, constant.numeric, function, comment
Selection & cursorui.selection, ui.cursor, ui.cursorline.primary, ui.linenr.selected
Diagnosticsdiagnostic.error / .warning / .info — plus `ui.virtual.wrap`? no: the gutter sign is drawn by Helix
Diffdiff.plus, diff.minus, diff.delta, diff.plus.gutter, diff.minus.gutter
Mode blocksui.statusline.normal / .insert / .select — the mode word plus its fill; visual mode is VIS, select mode is SEL
TerminalNot built in. Helix runs inside the terminal; terminal ANSI is configured by the emulator, not the theme
  • 01Tree-sitter captures only. Helix does not consume LSP semantic tokens, so `function` cannot distinguish a local closure from a method by token type alone.
  • 02No separate foreground for doc comments is guaranteed; the adapter maps comment.documentation and falls back to comment.
  • 03Truecolor support is required for every hex above. On a 256-colour terminal Helix quantises and the measured ratios no longer hold.
  • 04The active line number has its own key; the line number itself has none, so both resolve to muted.
  • 05Visual mode is a state, not a syntax colour. Approval of VIS rests on the mode word staying legible on its fill: bone on sage measures 5.42:1 in Paper, coal on sage 7.40:1 in Ink.

Zed

~/.config/zed/themes/lacuna.json, then `"theme": "Lacuna Ink"` in settings.json. The file is a theme family with two entries.

JSON with a `themes` array; each entry carries `name`, `appearance` and a flat `style` object of dot-named keys.

Colour valuesLiteral hex per key; Zed has no palette indirection inside a theme file
Document surfacebackground, text, text.muted, border, element.background
Syntaxsyntax.keyword, syntax.string, syntax.type, syntax.number, syntax.function, syntax.comment
Selection & cursorelement.selected, editor.highlighted_line.background, editor.document_highlight.read_background
Diagnosticserror, warning, info, hint — surfaced in the diagnostics panel and as underlines
Diffdiff.plus.background, diff.minus.background, diff.delta.background
Terminalterminal.background, terminal.foreground, terminal.ansi.red / green / yellow …
  • 01Zed resolves tree-sitter highlights and LSP semantic tokens. Semantic tokens win where the language server provides them, so `function.method` can differ from the same text in Helix.
  • 02`syntax.type` covers namespaces; Zed has no separate namespace key in the family schema used here.
  • 03ANSI colours have no blue or magenta in the Aporia palette. Both fall back to type ochre and chestnut and are flagged in Open items.
  • 04Family files are validated against the installed Zed build; unknown keys are ignored rather than rejected, so a silent fallback is possible.

Open items

  • Q1Real editor validationHelix and Zed need real host screenshots, syntax-capture QA and OS-theme switching checks. Generated HTML specimens are illustrations, not editor screenshots.
  • Q2Text selectionSelection is the canonical editor.selection token rather than reverse-video. Test multiline selections, selection text legibility and multiple cursors in each host.
  • Q3Host feature differencesHelix uses Tree-sitter captures; Zed can also use semantic tokens. Some colors depend on the active grammar and editor version.
  • Q4Truecolor and terminal palettesReal terminal colors may differ with 256-color quantization and display profiles. ANSI blue/magenta/cyan use the canonical utility roles, not a parallel theme palette.
  • Q5Fonts and shapingTheme files control color, not font fallback, ligatures, Persian shaping or terminal character-cell width. These remain host configuration concerns.

Handoff

  • 01Edit only the canonical treeEdit aporia/tokens.json; use aporia/RULES.md for intended semantics. Do not edit dist or generated previews.
  • 02Generate every platformRun npm run build. This resolves the same 79 color roles for Paper and Ink and produces all host themes and the gallery.
  • 03Validate and check driftRun npm test and npm run check:drift. Tests cover contrast, file structure, matrix completeness and determinism.
  • 04Install a host themeFollow docs/INSTALL.md to install Helix, Zed, VS Code, Kitty, Ghostty, Alacritty or WezTerm assets.
  • 05Test in the actual hostVisually test diagnostics, selections, diffs and syntax in a live editor or terminal; browser specimens are an approximation.

Lacuna — a family inside Aporia

Paper and Ink are one mapping in two editions. Aporia owns the identity; Lacuna carries it into editors and terminals. Nothing here was captured from Helix or Zed.
